name: Nomad
technique: Zero hash initialized as trusted root
rootCause: An upgrade initialized the trusted Merkle root to 0x00. Unproven messages map to root 0x00 by default, so every message counted as proven. Once the first attacker showed how, hundreds of copycats replayed the transaction with their own address: a "crowd-looted" bridge.

descriptions.text: An upgrade initialized the trusted Merkle root to 0x00. Unproven messages map to root 0x00 by default, so every message counted as proven. Once the first attacker showed how, hundreds of copycats replayed the transaction with their own address: a "crowd-looted" bridge.
Business Logic Flaw : Incorrect acceptable merkle-root checks. Lost: Multiple ERC-20 Tokens (~152M US$)

Nomad Bridge has been torn apart, with $190M drained in a savage attack. This is the 100th incident to make it onto the leaderboard, but DeFi still has plenty of easy prey, and scavengers continue to circle overhead.

business Logic Flaw, Incorrect acceptable merkle-root checks Nomad team initialized the trusted root to be 0x00. Vulnerable code snippet: https://etherscan.io/address/0xb92336759618f55bd0f8313bd843604592e27bd8#code Replica.sol ---

The Nomad Bridge, a cross-chain interoperability protocol, was attacked by hackers. This attack was due to the fact that the trusted root of the Nomad Bridge Replica contract was set to 0x0 during initialization, and the old root was not invalidated when the trusted root was modified. Constructing arbitrary messages to steal funds from the bridge, the attacker was able to extract over $190 million in value from the attack. So far, more than 40 addresses have returned over $36 million to Nomad.

Nomad's bridge lost approximately $190 million beginning August 1, 2022 UTC. A zero root accepted during an upgrade collided with the default mapping value for unproved messages, allowing forged withdrawals and copycat transactions to release bridge-held assets. Replica initialization pre-approved a zero committed root with confirmAt[0] = 1. Unproved messages also resolved to zero in the messages mapping. process() passed that default value to acceptableRoot(), which accepted it, allowing unauthenticated withdrawal instructions to reach the BridgeRouter.
